API keys are stored securely on the server. According to the documentation, 256-bit random keys are used, and SHA-256 is used for storage at rest. Additionally, per-key rate limits are implemented to prevent key guessing or brute force attacks. The API keys are also not stored in the browser, as the server-side sessions are used instead, and the cookie is set as `HttpOnly` to prevent JavaScript from accessing it.

{"question": "How are API keys stored on the server?"}

API keys are stored securely on the server. According to the documentation, 256-bit random keys are used, and SHA-256 is used for storage at rest. Additionally, per-key rate limits are implemented to prevent key guessing or brute force attacks. The API keys are also not stored in the browser, as the server-side sessions are used instead, and the cookie is set as `HttpOnly` to prevent JavaScript from accessing it.
